Geolocation

Privacy Detection

IPinfo Developer Resource

The quickest and easiest way to get started with IPinfo is to use one of our official libraries, which are available for many popular programming languages and frameworks. If you'd like to write your own library or interact directly with our API, then the documentation below can help you.

Authentication

Your API token is used to authenticate you with our API.

The IPinfo API endpoint supports authentication using any of the following methods:

  • A token query parameter (?token=$TOKEN)
  • HTTP Basic Authentication (using the token as the username, e.g. curl -u $TOKEN:)
  • A Bearer token in the Authorization header (Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN)

You can find your IPinfo API access token on your dashboard.

IPinfo Lite is our free tier API service available to all users. The API returns country and ASN information without any API request quota restrictions.

IPinfo Lite uses the api.ipinfo.io API URL and /lite endpoint.

Bash
# With token query parameter
$ curl https://api.ipinfo.io/lite/me?token=$TOKEN
$ curl https://api.ipinfo.io/lite/8.8.8.8?token=$TOKEN

# With Basic Auth
$ curl -u $TOKEN: https://api.ipinfo.io/lite/me
$ curl -u $TOKEN: https://api.ipinfo.io/lite/8.8.8.8

# With Bearer token
$ curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.ipinfo.io/lite/me
$ curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.ipinfo.io/lite/8.8.8.8
API Response
JSON
{
  "ip": "8.8.8.8",
  "asn": "AS15169",
  "as_name": "Google LLC",
  "as_domain": "google.com",
  "country_code": "US",
  "country": "United States",
  "continent_code": "NA",
  "continent": "North America"
}

IP Address Parameter

The API supports passing in a single IPv4 or IPv6 IP address. Alternatively, if you do not pass in any IP address, we'll return details for the calling address. This allows you to look up your own (or a visitor to your site) IP address details without knowing the IP address in advance.

URL Structure

The API follows a consistent URL structure with the following components:

ComponentDescriptionExamples
Base URLThe base domain for all API requestsapi.ipinfo.io
EndpointThe API version endpointlite (IPinfo Lite)
lookup (Core/Plus)
IP AddressThe IP to lookup (optional, defaults to requester's IP)me (your IP)
8.8.8.8 (IPv4)
2001:4860:4860::8888 (IPv6)
Field FilterOptional filter to return only specific fields (returned as plaintext)/country
/asn
/country_code
/is_proxy
TokenYour authentication token (query parameter)?token=$TOKEN

Example URLs:

https://api.ipinfo.io/lite/me?token=$TOKEN
https://api.ipinfo.io/lookup/8.8.8.8?token=$TOKEN
https://api.ipinfo.io/lite/2001:4860:4860::8888/country?token=$TOKEN
Bash
# Get details for 8.8.8.8
$ curl https://api.ipinfo.io/lite/8.8.8.8?token=$TOKEN

# Get details for 2001:4860:4860::8888
$ curl https://api.ipinfo.io/lite/2001:4860:4860::8888?token=$TOKEN

# Get details for your own IP address, which'll be included in the response
$ curl https://api.ipinfo.io/lite/me?token=$TOKEN

Our API is available over a secure HTTPS connection for all users. Simply add https:// to the request URLs to make the requests secure.

Rate Limits

IPinfo Lite offers unlimited access to our API. Paid plans include a monthly request limit with configurable alerts to help you stay in control. If you exceed your plan's limit, you'll receive a 429 HTTP status code. With metered billing enabled, usage continues uninterrupted via overages.

What is not limited:

  • No daily or hourly caps. You can use your full monthly quota in any pattern, including consuming it all within a single hour.
  • No concurrent request limits. There is no enforced cap on parallel requests. Our infrastructure routinely serves customers running hundreds of thousands of - requests per second.
  • No per-second throttling on paid plans. The monthly request count is the only volume constraint.

Filtering Responses

You can filter the API response down to specific fields or objects by adding the field or object name to the URL. In the case of a field you'll get it returned in plaintext, and an object will get returned as JSON.

Bash
# Get the ASN
$ curl https://api.ipinfo.io/lite/8.8.8.8/asn?token=$TOKEN
AS15169

# Get country ISO code as plaintext
$ curl https://api.ipinfo.io/lite/8.8.8.8/country_code?token=$TOKEN
US

Dual Stack API Service

Our API system is dual-stacked, making it easier for users on IPv6 connections. You can access the API seamlessly without needing to switch endpoints.

The examples below show how to force IPv4 or IPv6 connections using the -4 and -6 flags with curl.

On IPv4 Connection:

Bash
$ curl -4 https://api.ipinfo.io/lite/me?token=$TOKEN
API Response
JSON
{
  "ip": "102.135.36.0",
  "asn": "AS208485",
  "as_name": "Nese Mala trading as Moon Dc",
  "as_domain": "moondc.com",
  "country_code": "TR",
  "country": "Turkey",
  "continent_code": "AS",
  "continent": "Asia"
}

On IPv6 Connection:

Bash
$ curl -6 https://api.ipinfo.io/lite/me?token=$TOKEN
API Response
JSON
{
  "ip": "2602:f8de::",
  "asn": "AS53356",
  "as_name": "Free Range Cloud Hosting Inc.",
  "as_domain": "freerangecloud.com",
  "country_code": "US",
  "country": "United States",
  "continent_code": "NA",
  "continent": "North America"
}

Explicit IPv4 and IPv6 endpoint

For IPv4 connections, you can prepend the API endpoint with the subdomain v4.

Bash
$ curl https://v4.api.ipinfo.io/lite/me?token=$TOKEN
$ curl https://v4.api.ipinfo.io/lite/8.8.8.8?token=$TOKEN

For IPv6 connections, you can prepend the API endpoint with the subdomain v6.

Bash
$ curl https://v6.api.ipinfo.io/lite/me?token=$TOKEN
$ curl https://v6.api.ipinfo.io/lite/8.8.8.8?token=$TOKEN

JSONP/CORS Requests

JSONP and CORS are supported, allowing you to use ipinfo.io entirely in client-side code. For JSONP you just need to specify the callback parameter, e.g. http://ipinfo.io/?callback=callback&token=$TOKEN.

JavaScript
fetch("https://api.ipinfo.io/lite/me?token=$TOKEN")
  .then((response) => response.json())
  .then((jsonResponse) => console.log(jsonResponse.ip, jsonResponse.country));

Database Downloads

IPinfo's data is also available as downloadable databases (CSV, MMDB, JSON, and Parquet formats) that you can host offline and query yourself. Browse the available databases on the Database Types page, or head straight to Database Download for setup instructions.

  • Is there a minimum subscription period?
    No, you can cancel anytime you want. You can choose to subscribe on a month to month basis or choose our yearly subscription plans for additional savings.
  • What's included in the IPinfo Enterprise API response?

    IPinfo Enterprise is designed for customers with over 1 million requests per month who need greater scale and flexibility. Rather than changing the structure of the our API responses, the Enterprise plan gives you access to multiple standalone APIs that can be used together or individually.

    These include:

    • Geolocation & Privacy data
    • IP Ranges API
    • WHOIS Data API
    • Reverse Domains API
    • IPinfo Core API

    And other specialized endpoints.

    You can explore individual response formats in our developer docs, or get in touch to build the right setup for your business.

  • How will you track my requests?

    We track your API usage through your access token, which you include in each request. You can find your token in your dashboard. Your request volume is monitored against this token, and we’ll notify you by email as you approach your monthly plan limit — and again if you reach it.

  • How can I keep an eye on my request volumes?
    We display a graph of your request volumes that updates real-time. You can view your requests by heading to your Dashboard. We also send a weekly summary email about the requests you've made.
  • How reliable is IPinfo’s API?

    IPinfo’s API is built for performance at scale, with 99.99% uptime and average response times of 50–200 ms. It supports up to 100,000 queries per second, making it a robust solution for real-time applications and enterprise-grade workloads. In the past year alone, we’ve processed over 1.95 trillion API requests, a reflection of the reliability and trust our infrastructure provides to developers and businesses worldwide.

  • What if I only go a few hundred requests over my quota? How much will it cost?

    We bill each extra request at your plan’s exact PPQ (price-per-query) and round the month-end total to the nearest cent. Current PPQs are:

    • Core: $0.000539 per request
    • Plus: $0.000811 per request
    • Max: $0.001030 per request
    Example (IPinfo Core plan)

    237 extra requests × $0.000539 = $0.127543 → rounded on your invoice to $0.13.

    So whether you exceed your quota by 1 request or 999, you’re charged only for the traffic you actually send, never a full block.

  • Can I download your IP data as a database?

    Yes, IPinfo data is available as a downloadable database. However, this option is not included in self-serve plans. To access the database download, please contact our sales team for more information and pricing.
